approachQuestion.prompt:
Sum Two Reverse-Written Counters

Two nonempty finite acyclic singly linked lists store decimal digits least significant first. Each encodes a nonnegative integer, with no zero at its most significant end unless the entire list is the single digit 0. Return a newly allocated list in the same representation for their sum; do not change inputs or refer to their nodes from the result. Arbitrarily long integers are unavailable; machine-word arithmetic on individual digits is constant-time. Let n and m be input lengths, 1 <= n,m <= 200000.

Input: [8,9] and [7,1,2], representing 98 and 217. Output: [5,1,3], representing 315.
Input: [9] and [1]. Output: [0,1].

Choose a method that satisfies the full contract with the best worst-case running time, breaking time ties by least auxiliary storage.

options.text: Copy both digit sequences into arrays, add by increasing index with the same carry rule, and build a fresh result chain.
options.feedback: The digit arithmetic is correct, but copying inputs into arrays is unnecessary storage.

options.text: Add aligned digits modulo ten and never carry into the next position.
Use digit-wise carry addition but stop as soon as either input ends.
options.feedback: [1] plus [0,2] must produce [1,2]; stopping after the first position loses the remaining 2.

options.text: Walk both digit chains with a carry. Treat an exhausted chain's digit as zero. Append a new node holding sum modulo ten, update carry by integer division by ten, and continue until both chains and carry are exhausted.
options.feedback: Each step emits the next least significant result digit and carries exactly the remaining tens into the next position.

feedback.reason: Each step emits the next least significant result digit and carries exactly the remaining tens into the next position.
details: Walk both digit chains with a carry. Treat an exhausted chain's digit as zero. Append a new node holding sum modulo ten, update carry by integer division by ten, and continue until both chains and carry are exhausted.

Least-significant digits arrive first, so carry propagates naturally along the lists. Treat an exhausted input as zero and keep processing a final carry. New digit nodes are required output, not a helper copy of whole integers.

“Add aligned digits modulo ten and never carry into the next position.”: [9] plus [1] produces [0] instead of [0,1].
“Use digit-wise carry addition but stop as soon as either input ends.”: [1] plus [0,2] must produce [1,2]; stopping after the first position loses the remaining 2.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only the revealed method (acm-b15-17-target), regardless of your Q1 choice. Here n and m are the two input lengths. Choose the tight worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Count each node allocation, link access, identity/value comparison and machine-word operation as constant work. Include all temporary collections and call frames; exclude supplied nodes and the final returned output only. Copying or allocating k records costs k operations. No hash-table, amortized-operation or tail-call assumptions are used.

options.explanation: This pair does not describe the fixed method. Each supplied digit is read once, with at most one extra carry digit. The result contains at most max(n,m)+1 newly allocated nodes, whose construction is included in time but whose storage is output and excluded from auxiliary space. Only fixed references and a digit-sized carry are auxiliary. No whole-number copies, collections or recursion occur.
